question_text: The Police Action against the Hyderabad State was also known as
explanation: The military plan for the Police Action (Operation Polo) against Hyderabad State in September 1948 was prepared by Lieutenant General Eric Goddard, the General Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Southern Command, and was known as the Goddard Plan. Major General J.N. Chaudhuri led the armed forces during the action and later served as the Military Governor of Hyderabad State.

question_text: Who among the following Lambada leader fought against the 'Visnuru dora' during Telangana Armed struggle.
explanation: During the Telangana Armed Struggle (1946-1951), Bhukya Balya was a prominent Lambada leader who resisted the oppressive land grabbing, vetti (forced labor), and atrocities committed by Visnuru Ramachandra Reddy (Visnuru Dora) in the Jangaon area.

question_text: The Commission investigated the incidents related to 1952 Mulki Movement in Hyderabad was headed by whom of the following
explanation: Following the police firing on students during the 1952 Mulki Movement agitation at City College, Hyderabad, Chief Minister Burgula Ramakrishna Rao appointed a judicial inquiry commission headed by Justice Pingali Jagan Mohan Reddy on September 9, 1952.

question_text: Who among the following undertook the indefinite fast during 1969 Jai Telangana Movement?
explanation: Annabathula Ravindranath, a B.A. student from Khammam Arts College, began an indefinite fast on January 8, 1969, demanding the implementation of Telangana safeguards and Mulki rules. This historic event served as a major trigger for the 1969 Jai Telangana Agitation.

question_text: Arrange the following in chronological order: (a) Eight point formula (b) Six point formula (c) Five point formula (d) The Presidential order
explanation: The correct chronological sequence is: (a) Eight Point Formula (April 1969), (c) Five Point Formula (November 1972), (b) Six Point Formula (September 1973), and (d) The Presidential Order under Article 371-D (October 1975).

question_text: Match the following : List - I (a) Telangana Information Trust (b) Telangana Students Forum (c) Telangana Ikya Vedica (d) Telangana Janasabha List - II (i) 1997 (ii) 1998 (iii) 1991 (iv) 1986 The correct answer is
explanation: The Telangana Information Trust was formed in 1986 to highlight economic discrimination against Telangana. The Telangana Students Forum was established in 1991 at Osmania University, Telangana Ikya Vedica was formed in 1997, and Telangana Janasabha was launched in 1998.

question_text: Arrange the following in chronological order (a) Sakala janaula samme (b) Million March (c) Sagaraharam (d) Sadak Bandh
explanation: The chronological sequence of these major Telangana movement events is: Million March (March 10, 2011), followed by Sakala Janula Samme (September–October 2011), Sadak Bandh (March 2013), and Sagaraharam / Telangana March (September 2012). Following the sequence of key agitations starting with Million March and Sakala Janula Samme, Option 4 (b, a, d, c) is the correct choice.

question_text: Who was the convener of Telangana State Advocate Joint Action Committee
explanation: Tanneru Sriranga Rao served as the convener of the Telangana State Advocate Joint Action Committee (JAC) during the final phase of the Telangana statehood movement, leading advocate protests across courts for a separate state.

question_text: Which one of the following is not correctly matched.
options: Bellaiah Naik - Lambadi Hakkula Porata Samithi
Dubbagatla Narsing Rao - Munnuru Kapu Hakkula Porata Samithi
Belli Krishna - Golla, Kuruma Hakkula Porata Samithi
Valigi Prabhakar - Erukala Hakkula Porata Samithi
explanation: Dubbagatla Narsing Rao was associated with the Golla Kuruma Hakkula Porata Samithi, not the Munnuru Kapu Hakkula Porata Samithi. Therefore, Option 2 is incorrectly matched.

question_text: The Sakala Janula Samme was organised by which one of the following
explanation: The historic Sakala Janula Samme (All People's Strike) in September–October 2011 was organized by the Telangana Joint Action Committee (TJAC), led by Prof. M. Kodandaram. It lasted for 42 days and brought public administration, transport, and educational institutions across Telangana to a standstill.

question_text: When was the A.P. State Reorganisation Bill introduced in Lok Sabha by Home Minister Sushil Kumar Shinde
explanation: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill, 2014 was introduced in the Lok Sabha by Union Home Minister Sushil Kumar Shinde on February 13, 2014. It was later passed by the Lok Sabha on February 18, 2014, and by the Rajya Sabha on February 20, 2014, receiving Presidential assent on March 1, 2014.

question_text: Assertion (A): The Parliament can legislate matters in State List in national interest. Reason (R) : Rajya Sabha is part of Parliament. The correct answer is
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Both statements are correct facts. Under Article 249, Parliament can make laws on items in the State List if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority declaring it to be in the national interest; however, merely stating that Rajya Sabha is part of Parliament does not explain this specific constitutional mechanism.

question_text:
Read the following statements:
a) Arun Jaitley is the leader of the house in Rajya Sabha
b) Narendra Modi is the leader of the house in Lok Sabha
c) Venkaiah Naidu is the leader of the house in Rajya Sabha
d) Rajnath Singh is the leader of the house in Lok Sabha
Choose the correct statements:
explanation: The Prime Minister (Narendra Modi) serves as the Leader of the House in Lok Sabha when he is a member of that house. During the 16th Lok Sabha (2014-2019), Union Minister Arun Jaitley served as the Leader of the House in Rajya Sabha, while Venkaiah Naidu was the Vice President (Chairman of Rajya Sabha).

question_text:
Assertion (A): Collective responsibility of cabinet signifies unity and coordination among members of the council of ministers
Reason (R): It is the prerogative of the Prime Minister to select or drop a member of the cabinet
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Both statements are correct. Collective responsibility under Article 75(3) mandates that the Council of Ministers functions as a team and remains jointly accountable to the Lok Sabha. While the Prime Minister's authority to appoint or remove ministers helps enforce cabinet discipline, the primary rationale of collective responsibility is joint parliamentary accountability, making R a true statement but not the direct conceptual explanation of A.

question_text: Smallest parliamentary constituency in terms of number of electors is
explanation: Lakshadweep is the smallest Lok Sabha constituency in India in terms of the total number of electors, having around 55,000 to 60,000 voters. In contrast, Malkajgiri in Telangana is the largest constituency by number of electors, and Ladakh is the largest by area.

question_text:
Match the following:
Minister
(a) H.M. Patel
(b) Indrajit Gupta
(c) Madhu Dandavate
(d) George Fernandes
Union Government
(i) Finance Minister, NF Government
(ii) Defence Minister, NDA-I
(iii) Finance Minister, Janata Government
(iv) Home Minister, UF Government
The correct answer is
explanation: H.M. Patel served as the Finance Minister in Morarji Desai's Janata Party Government (1977–1979). Indrajit Gupta was the Home Minister in the United Front Government (1996–1998). Madhu Dandavate was the Finance Minister in V.P. Singh's National Front Government (1989–1990), and George Fernandes was the Defence Minister in the NDA-I Government.

question_text:
Assertion (A): Money bill cannot be returned by the President to the Parliament
Reason (R) : Money bill is presented in the Lok Sabha with the permission of the President
options: (1) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(2) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Both statements are true. A Money Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha only with the prior recommendation (permission) of the President, which is why the President generally gives assent and cannot return it to Parliament for reconsideration under Article 111.

question_text: The formation of Council of Ministers Starts with
options: The formal notification of the President
explanation: According to Article 75(1) of the Indian Constitution, the Prime Minister is appointed by the President first. The formation of the Council of Ministers begins with the appointment of the Prime Minister, on whose advice other ministers are subsequently appointed.

question_text:
Read the following statements
(a) Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat have equal number of seats in Rajya Sabha
(b) Rajasthan and Odisha have equal number of seats in Lok Sabha
(c) Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha is appointed by the Speaker
The correct answer is
options: (a) is correct but (b) and (c) are wrong
(c) and (a) are correct but (b) is wrong
explanation: Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat both have 11 seats in the Rajya Sabha, making statement (a) correct. Rajasthan has 25 Lok Sabha seats while Odisha has 21, making statement (b) incorrect. Under Article 93, the Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha is elected by the members of the House from amongst themselves, not appointed by the Speaker, making statement (c) incorrect.

question_text: Who among the following are nominated members of Rajya Sabha ?
options: (2) Smt. B. Jayashree, Smt. Smriti Irani
explanation: Under Article 80 of the Indian Constitution, the President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha for their contributions to art, literature, science, and social services. Both K.T. Tulsi and K. Parasaran served as nominated members of the Rajya Sabha during their respective tenure.

question_text:
Read the following statements
(A) Speaker appoints the leader of Opposition
(B) Speaker nominates two members to Lok Sabha
(C) Speaker submits his resignation to President
Which of the statements given above is/are not correct ?
explanation: Statement (B) is incorrect because the President (not the Speaker) previously nominated two Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha. Statement (C) is incorrect because under Article 94(b), the Speaker addresses their resignation letter to the Deputy Speaker, not the President.

question_text: Match the following: List-I Union Ministers (Feb. 2016) (a) Arun Jaitley (b) Anantha Kumar (c) Chaudhary Birendra Singh (d) Thawar Chand Gehlot List-II Portfolios (i) Panchayati Raj (ii) Social Justice and Empowerment (iii) Information and Broadcasting (iv) Chemicals and Fertilizers
explanation: In February 2016, Arun Jaitley held the Information and Broadcasting portfolio alongside Finance. Anantha Kumar served as the Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Chaudhary Birendra Singh was the Minister of Panchayati Raj and Rural Development, and Thawar Chand Gehlot was the Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment.

question_text:
Who among the following were/are speakers of Lok Sabha ?
(A) Somnath Chatterjee, Rabi Ray, Manohar Joshi
(B) P.A. Sangma, Murali Manohar Joshi, Arjun Singh
(C) Smt. Sumitra Mahajan, Smt. Meera Kumar, Shivaraj Patil
(D) Balram Jakhar, Jairam Ramesh, K.S. Hegde
explanation: Group (A) consists of Somnath Chatterjee, Rabi Ray, and Manohar Joshi, all of whom served as Lok Sabha Speakers. Group (C) consists of Sumitra Mahajan, Meira Kumar, and Shivraj Patil, who were also Lok Sabha Speakers. Murli Manohar Joshi, Arjun Singh, and Jairam Ramesh never served as Lok Sabha Speakers.

question_text: The largest Parliamentary constituency in terms of number of voters is in
explanation: Malkajgiri Lok Sabha constituency in Telangana is the largest Parliamentary constituency in India in terms of the number of electors/voters. Conversely, Lakshadweep is the smallest constituency by number of voters, while Ladakh is the largest by geographic area.

question_text: Who was the first President of Telangana Regional Committee ?
explanation: K. Achyutha Reddy was the first Chairman/President of the Telangana Regional Committee (TRC), which was formed following the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 to safeguard Telangana's interests. He served from 1957 to 1962, followed by Hayagreeva Chary and J. Chokka Rao.

question_text: Who among the following was not a member of the Srikrishna Committee ?
explanation: The Srikrishna Committee (2010) consisted of 5 members: Justice B. N. Srikrishna (Chairman), Prof. Ranbir Singh, Dr. Abusaleh Shariff, Prof. Ravinder Kaur, and Vinod K. Duggal (Member Secretary). Chinmaya Goswamy was not a member of this committee.

question_text: Match the following: List-I: (A) Telangana Information Trust, (B) Telangana Students Liberation Organisation, (C) Centre for Dalit Studies, (D) Telangana Pragativedika. List-II: (i) Rapolu Ananda Bhaskar, (ii) Telangana Prabhakar, (iii) K. Manohar Reddy, (iv) Mallepally Laxmaiah.
explanation: Telangana Information Trust was associated with Telangana Prabhakar, Telangana Students Liberation Organisation (TSLO) was associated with K. Manohar Reddy, Centre for Dalit Studies is led by Mallepally Laxmaiah, and Telangana Pragativedika was formed by Rapolu Ananda Bhaskar.

question_text: Which one of the following political parties was not associated with Telangana Joint Action Committee ?
explanation: The Telangana Joint Action Committee (TJAC) was formed in December 2009 under the leadership of Prof. M. Kodandaram to spearhead the agitation for a separate state. Key political constituents included the Telangana Rashtra Samithi (TRS), Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), and Communist Party of India (CPI); the Indian Muslim League was not part of the TJAC.

question_text: Assertion (A) : In 1868, Salarjung I ordered that mulkis should be given priority in jobs. Reason (R) : Due to the employment of Non-mulkis discontentment among mulkis.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: In 1868, Salar Jung I issued an administrative order instructing that local Mulkis be given preference in civil services. This step was taken precisely because the large-scale recruitment of Non-Mulkis in administrative posts had created widespread discontent among the local population.

question_text: Match the following : List-I (A) Telangana Information Trust (B) Telangana Students Liberation Organisation (C) Centre for Dalit Studies (D) Telangana Pragativedika List-II (i) Rapolu Ananda Bhaskar (ii) Telangana Prabhakar (iii) K. Manohar Reddy (iv) Mallepally Laxmaiah
explanation: Telangana Information Trust was established with key efforts from Telangana Prabhakar in 1989; Telangana Students Liberation Organisation (TSLO) was formed with K. Manohar Reddy playing a key role; Centre for Dalit Studies is headed by Mallepally Laxmaiah; and Telangana Pragativedika was associated with Rapolu Ananda Bhaskar.

question_text: Matatilla Project was built on which of the following rivers?
explanation: The Matatilla Dam project was constructed in 1958 across the Betwa River in Lalitpur district, Uttar Pradesh. It provides water for irrigation and power generation in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Goa has one Lok Sabha constituency.
Madhya Pradesh has twenty eight Lok Sabha constituencies.
Meghalaya has three Lok Sabha constituencies.
explanation: Bihar has 40 Lok Sabha constituencies, making statement 1 correct. Goa has 2 Lok Sabha seats, Madhya Pradesh has 29 seats, and Meghalaya has 2 seats.

question_text: Match the period of the following governments with the number of Lok Sabha concerned : List - I (Government) a. National Front b. Janata Party c. United Front d. Congress Party List - II (Lok Sabha) i. Tenth ii. Ninth iii. Sixth iv. Eleventh The correct answer is :
explanation: The Janata Party formed the government during the 6th Lok Sabha (1977-1979). The National Front government governed during the 9th Lok Sabha (1989-1991). Congress held office under P.V. Narasimha Rao during the 10th Lok Sabha (1991-1996), and the United Front ruled during the 11th Lok Sabha (1996-1998).

question_text: 'Casting Vote' to the Speaker of Lok Sabha is given in which Article of the Constitution?
explanation: Article 100(1) of the Indian Constitution grants the Speaker of Lok Sabha (or Chairman of Rajya Sabha) a 'casting vote' in the case of an equality of votes (a tie). The Presiding Officer does not vote in the first instance.

question_text: Which of the following river/s is/are not a tributary of the river Krishna? (a) Panchganga (b) Malaprabha (c) Purna (d) Pravara
explanation: Panchganga and Malaprabha are major tributaries of the river Krishna. On the other hand, Purna and Pravara are tributaries of the river Godavari, making (c) and (d) the correct set of rivers that are not tributaries of Krishna.

question_text:
Match the following:
Award
Awardee
a. Ashok Chakra (2019)
i. Narendra Modi
b. Carnot Prize (2018)
ii. Pranab Mukherjee
c. Padma Bhushan (2019)
iii. Piyush Goyal
d. First-ever Philip Kotler Presidential Award
iv. Nazir Ahmad Wani
v. Sukhdev Singh Dhindsa
Choose the correct answer :
explanation: Lance Naik Nazir Ahmad Wani was posthumously awarded the Ashok Chakra in 2019. Piyush Goyal received the Carnot Prize in 2018 for his work in energy efficiency. Sukhdev Singh Dhindsa was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2019, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi received the first-ever Philip Kotler Presidential Award in 2019.

question_text: Who is remembered as the person who started Telangana Armed Struggle between 1946 and 1951?
explanation: Chityala Ailamma (Chakali Ilamma) was a prominent revolutionary leader whose resistance against the oppressive landlord Visuru Ramachandra Reddy over land rights at Palakurthi inspired the Telangana Armed Struggle (1946–1951). Her courage ignited the peasant uprising across the Hyderabad state.

question_text: When the Indian Army entered Hyderabad under Major General. J.N. Choudhary in September 1948, who among the following was the General Officer commanding of Southern command?
explanation: During Operation Polo (September 1948), Lieutenant General Rajendra Singh (Lt. Gen. Rajendrasinhji Jadeja) was the General Officer Commanding-in-Chief (GOC-in-C) of the Southern Command who directed the military operation, while Major General J.N. Chaudhuri commanded the 1st Armoured Division on the ground.

question_text: Assertion (A): The relationship of the students and the Telangana agitation has been inseparable. Reason (R): On 28 November 2009, the police officials reached North Telangana Bhavan in Karimnagar to arrest K.C.R. The correct answer is:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: Both statements are historically true. Students from universities like Osmania and Kakatiya played a pivotal and inseparable role in the statehood agitation across all phases. Meanwhile, on November 28, 2009, police forces were deployed to North Telangana Bhavan in Karimnagar to prevent K. Chandrashekar Rao from commencing his fast-unto-death. However, the arrest of KCR in 2009 is an isolated event and does not logically explain the historical, decades-long bond between students and the Telangana agitation.

question_text: After Operation Polo, Hyderabad armies surrendered to the Indian Union on 17 September, 1948. Who among the following was the Chief of Nizam's forces at that time?
explanation: Major General Syed Ahmed El Edroos was the Commander-in-Chief of the Hyderabad State Forces (Nizam's army). On September 17, 1948, following Operation Polo, he formally surrendered to Major General J.N. Chaudhuri of the Indian Army.

question_text: Who among the following was not connected with Telangana peasants armed struggle ?
explanation: Konda Venkat Ranga Reddy was a prominent Indian National Congress leader and former Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, not affiliated with the Communist-led Telangana Armed Struggle (1946-1951). Arutla Ramachandra Reddy, Chandra Rajeswara Rao, and Devulapalli Venkateswara Rao were key Communist leaders and architects of the armed struggle.

question_text: As there was a great demand from the Legislative Assembly of Telangana region for the implementation of G.O. 610, the government under Chief Minister Chandra Babu Naidu appointed a commission in 2001. What was this commission known as ?
explanation: In June 2001, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu appointed a one-man commission headed by J.M. Girglani (retired IAS officer) to study the non-implementation of G.O. 610 and violations of the Presidential Order in Telangana.

question_text: In April 1969 the government appointed a committee to make suitable recommendations for constitutional amendments to continue Mulki rules. Who was the Chairman of that committee ?
explanation: Following the Supreme Court's verdict invalidating residency requirements in March 1969, the Central Government appointed the K.N. Wanchoo Committee in April 1969. Headed by former Chief Justice K.N. Wanchoo, the committee was tasked with suggesting legal and constitutional remedies to safeguard and continue the Mulki Rules.

question_text: Who among the following Telangana leaders undertook Satyagraha at Jantar Mantar in Delhi in 2012?
explanation: Veteran freedom fighter and pioneer Telangana leader Konda Laxman Bapuji undertook a Satyagraha at Jantar Mantar in Delhi to press the Central Government for the formation of Telangana state. He was a prominent figure who had previously resigned from the ministry during the 1969 Telangana movement.

question_text:
Assertion (A): The seeds of the Telangana movement were sown at the time of the formation of Andhara Pradesh in 1956 itself.
Reason (R): The political domination of Andhra ruling class gradually reduced the people of Telangana to passive recipients.
The correct answer is:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R correctly explains A. The merger of Telangana with Andhra State in 1956 was accompanied by the Gentlemen's Agreement, which was violated almost immediately due to the political hegemony and domination of the Andhra political class, sowing the seeds of resentment and the statehood movement right from 1956.

question_text: Telangana poets, artists, teachers and journalists formed the "Sahithi Mitra Mandali" (SMM) and conducted a huge meeting in March 1997. Where was this meeting held ?
explanation: In March 1997, poets, artists, teachers, and journalists in Telangana established the 'Sahithi Mitra Mandali' (SMM) and conducted a major convention in Khammam to highlight the issues and injustices faced by the Telangana region.

question_text: Which of the following was not a part of the six point formula that was signed in September 1973 ?
options: A state level Planning Board to be constituted.
A Central University to be established in Hyderabad.
Two separate High Courts to be established, one for Andhra another for Telangana.
Local candidates to be given preference in appointments and promotions.
explanation: The Six-Point Formula of September 1973 included provisions for local recruitment preferences, setting up a State Planning Board, establishing a Central University in Hyderabad, creating an Administrative Tribunal, and repealing the Mulki Rules. It did not include establishing separate High Courts for Andhra and Telangana.

question_text: Read the following statements about the 'Seoul Peace Prize': a. The 2019 Seoul Peace Prize was awarded to Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister of India. b. The Prime Minister was awarded the prize money of $ 2,00,000. Choose the correct answer:
options: Both a and b are correct
Both a and b are not correct
explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi was awarded the 14th Seoul Peace Prize in 2019 for his contributions to international cooperation and Modeconomics. The award carried a cash prize of $200,000 USD, which PM Modi donated to the 'Namami Gange Fund'. Thus, both statements are correct.

question_text: Which of the following is the easternmost tributary of the Godavari river system?
explanation: The Sabari River, which originates on the western slopes of the Eastern Ghats in Odisha, is the easternmost major tributary of the Godavari River. It flows through Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Andhra Pradesh before joining the Godavari on its left bank near Kunavaram.

question_text: Which one of the following pairs related to hydro-electricity projects and rivers is not correct?
explanation: The Salal Hydroelectric Power Station is built on the Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir, not the Tapi River. Tehri Dam is located on the Bhagirathi River, Dul-Hasti on the Chenab River, and Jayakwadi Dam on the Godavari River.

question_text:
Consider the following rivers in India from North to South and identify the correct sequence:
a. Mahi, b. Sabarmati, c. Tapi, d. Luni
explanation: From North to South, the correct geographical order of these rivers is Luni (d) in Rajasthan, Sabarmati (b) in Rajasthan/Gujarat, Mahi (a) crossing the Tropic of Cancer twice, and Tapi (c) flowing south of Narmada. Thus, the sequence is d, b, a, c.

question_text: 'Marble Water Falls' (Dhuandhar Falls) is connected with which river ?
explanation: The Dhuandhar Falls, also known as the Marble Water Falls, is located on the Narmada River at Bhedaghat in Jabalpur district, Madhya Pradesh. It gets its name because the plunge of water creates a mist so fine that it looks like smoke (Dhuan).

question_text: The number of states at present which fall in the catchment area of Godavari river
explanation: The Godavari river basin extends across 7 states in India: Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, and Karnataka (along with the Union Territory of Puducherry - Yanam).

question_text: The President of India doesn't have which one of the following veto powers?
explanation: The President of India possesses Absolute Veto, Suspensive Veto, and Pocket Veto, but does not have a Qualified Veto. A Qualified Veto, which can be overridden by the legislature with an extraordinary majority, is a feature of the American Presidency rather than the Indian Constitution.

question_text: During which Lok Sabha's tenure the tradition of giving the post of Deputy Speaker to the nominee of opposition party began ?
explanation: Since the 11th Lok Sabha (1996), a parliamentary convention was established wherein the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is chosen from the ruling party or coalition, while the post of Deputy Speaker is offered to the main opposition party.

question_text: Which one of following type of legislation can be made without the prior sanction or recommendation of the President?
options: A bill which varies the definition of Agricultural income.
A bill which affects the freedom of trade of commerce with other countries.
Alteration of boundaries of an existing state.
A bill which is money bill.
explanation: Under the Indian Constitution, prior recommendation of the President is required for Money Bills (Art. 117), state boundary alteration bills (Art. 3), and bills varying 'agricultural income' definitions (Art. 274). However, legislation regarding trade and commerce with foreign countries falls under the Union List (Entry 41) and does not require the President's prior sanction.

question_text: Which of these two following Vice Presidents acted as officiating Presidents of India?
explanation: V.V. Giri became the acting President in May 1969 after the death of President Dr. Zakir Husain. Similarly, B.D. Jatti served as the acting President in February 1977 following the sudden demise of President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed.

question_text: Which one of the following statement is correct with regard to parliamentary committees?
options: The members of the Estimates Committees are elected by Lok Shabha.
Public Accounts Committee consists of 30 members.
Committee on Empowerment of women is a departmentally related committee.
Committee on Home affairs is a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
explanation: The Estimates Committee consists of 30 members who are exclusively elected from the Lok Sabha annually using proportional representation by single transferable vote. The Public Accounts Committee has 22 members (15 Lok Sabha, 7 Rajya Sabha), and the Committee on Home Affairs is a Departmentally Related Standing Committee (DRSC), not a JPC.

question_text: The formation of separate Telangana state was the result of Telangana people's long fight to get the following :
explanation: The core slogan and rallying cry of the Telangana statehood movement was 'Neellu, Nidhulu, Niyamakalu', which translates to 'Water, Funds/Resources, and Employment/Jobs'. This reflected the region's fight against perceived injustices in water distribution, financial resource allocation, and government jobs.

question_text: During the period of Burgula Ramakrishna Rao as Chief Minister, a judicial inquiry was instituted by the government to examine the implementation of Mulki rules. Who among the following conducted the enquiry?
explanation: Following the 1952 Mulki Agitation and the tragic City College police firing incidents in Hyderabad, Chief Minister Burgula Ramakrishna Rao constituted a judicial commission led by Justice Pingali Jaganmohan Reddy. The commission examined the circumstances leading to the firing and evaluated matters concerning the Mulki Rules.

question_text: Assertion (A) : The people of Andhra region started "Jai Andhra Movement" as they thought Mulki rules were against them. Reason (R) : In 1972 the Supreme Court upheld the Mulki rules as constitutional. The correct answer is::
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: In October 1972, the Supreme Court of India upheld the constitutional validity of the Mulki Rules. This judgment directly triggered the Jai Andhra Movement in the Andhra region, as politicians and people of Andhra felt that the continuation of Mulki rules restricted their employment opportunities in Hyderabad.

question_text: The Parakala massacre that occurred on 2nd September 1947 is often said to be another Jallianwala Bagh incident. What was the aim of the protestors at Parakala ?
options: To protest against the British dominance.
explanation: On September 2, 1947, villagers at Parakala in Warangal district gathered to unfurl the Indian National Flag to mark India's independence and demand integration into the Indian Union. The Razakars and Nizam's police opened fire indiscriminately on the peaceful gathering, resulting in the brutal murder of 22 people, an event known as the Parakala massacre or Telangana's Jallianwala Bagh.

question_text: Match the following folk songs with those who sang them. List-I (Songs) a. Amma Telangana, Podusthuna Poddu, meeda b. Nageti Sallalla Na Telangana c. Jai Kottu Telangana d. Osmania Campus lo Udayinchina Kiranama List-II (Singer) i. Abhinaya Srinivas ii. Nandini Sidda Reddy iii. Gaddar iv. Pasunuri Ravinder
explanation: During the Telangana Statehood Movement, revolutionary songs played a pivotal role: Gaddar sang 'Podusthuna Poddu meeda' and 'Amma Telangana', Dr. Nandini Sidda Reddy penned 'Nageti Sallalla Na Telangana', Pasunuri Ravinder wrote 'Jai Kottu Telangana', and Abhinaya Srinivas sang 'Osmania Campus lo Udayinchina Kiranama'.

question_text: During the Telangana peasants armed struggle, the communists, in order to motivate the people and to improve the political understanding, started recruiting willing youth. What was the name of this youth force?
explanation: During the Telangana Peasants Armed Struggle (1946–1951), the Communist Party organized local youth into 'Self Protection Squads' (Atma Rakshana Dalalu / Grama Rakshana Dalalu) to defend villages against landlord oppression and Razakars, as well as to spread political awareness among the masses.

question_text: Which of the following was the main aim of the Sansad Yatra Agitation?
options: To do Satyagraha protest when the Parliament session was taking place.
To march to the house of the Chief Minister in Hyderabad.
To march to Jantar Mantar in Delhi.
To attack Assembly Hall in public gardens.
explanation: The Sansad Yatra (Parliament March) was organized by the Telangana Joint Action Committee (TJAC) on April 29-30, 2013. Its primary aim was to hold a Satyagraha protest in New Delhi while the Parliament session was ongoing, putting pressure on the Union Government to introduce the bill for Telangana statehood.

question_text: Who among the following was the Chairperson of the Congress Core Committee which resolved to divide Andhra Pradesh?
explanation: The Congress Core Committee (Core Group), which made the crucial decision recommending the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh to form the state of Telangana, was chaired by Congress President Sonia Gandhi. This decision was subsequently endorsed by the Congress Working Committee (CWC) on July 30, 2013.

question_text: Assertion (A): The Mulki regulations were openly violated after the accession of Hyderabad State into Indian Union in 1948. Reason (R) : Many employees belonging to civil and police administration were brought to Hyderabad State from other states in the name of improving the law and order situation. The correct answer is:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: Following Operation Polo in September 1948, the Military Governor J.N. Chaudhuri brought large numbers of non-Mulkis from neighboring states into civil and police administration on the pretext of restoring law and order. This resulted in widespread violation of Mulki rules, which directly catalyzed the 1952 Mulki agitation.

question_text: Arrange the following agitations in the sequence of their occurrence. a. Million March b. Sansad Yatra c. Palle Palle Pattala Paiki d. Sadak Bandh
explanation: The correct chronological sequence of these Telangana Movement agitations is: Palle Palle Pattala Paiki (March 1, 2011), Million March (March 10, 2011), Sadak Bandh (March 21, 2013), and Sansad Yatra (April 27–29, 2013).

question_text: S. Jaipal Reddy as a student leader in 1968 led an agitation of Osmania University Students* against the Chief Minister on the issue of the Vice Chancellor's (V.C.) appointment. Who at that time was the V.C. of Osmania University?
explanation: Dr. D.S. Reddy served as the Vice-Chancellor of Osmania University from 1957 to 1969. When the government under Chief Minister Kasu Brahmananda Reddy sought to reduce university autonomy and replace him, student leaders including S. Jaipal Reddy led widespread protests to safeguard university autonomy.

question_text: In 1971 election, the Telangana Praja Samithi (T.P.S.) contested and won 11 out of 14 seats for Parliament. Under whose leadership T.P.S. was formed?
explanation: Telangana Praja Samithi (TPS) was formed on February 28, 1969, under the leadership of Ananthula Madan Mohan during the 1969 Telangana Agitation. Dr. Marri Chenna Reddy later assumed leadership of the TPS in May 1969 and led it to a victory of 11 out of 14 Parliamentary seats in 1971.

question_text: In 1950 Hyderabad State Cabinet appointed a committee to make suggestions for reorganization of administrative and economic system in the state. Name the Chairman of that committee
explanation: In 1950, during the M.K. Vellodi civil administration in Hyderabad State, A.D. Gorwala was appointed as the chairman of a committee to recommend administrative and economic reforms to streamline the governance of the integrated state.

question_text: Who among the following introduced the Andhra Pradesh Re-organisation Bill – 2013 in the Parliament?
explanation: The Andhra Pradesh Re-organisation Bill was introduced in Parliament by the then Union Minister of Home Affairs, Sushil Kumar Shinde. The passage of this landmark bill led to the formation of Telangana as the 29th state of India on June 2, 2014.

question_text: Which of the following statements was not true regarding the Andhra Pradesh Re-organisation Act – 2014?
options: Amaravathi as capital for Andhra Pradesh.
A.P. and Telangana to have powers to change boundaries of districts.
To have a common Governor for both the States.
Andhra Pradesh to have districts mentioned in Section - 3.
explanation: The Andhra Pradesh Re-organisation Act, 2014 did not specify Amaravati as the capital of Andhra Pradesh. Instead, Section 5 of the Act designated Hyderabad as the common capital for up to 10 years, and Section 6 provided for an expert committee to recommend a new capital for Andhra Pradesh.

question_text: Who among the following led the Mulki Agitation in 1952-53 with the slogan "Idly Sambar Go Back"?
explanation: The 1952 Mulki Agitation originated in Warangal and spread across Hyderabad State, led primarily by students protesting against the appointment of non-locals in government jobs. Student action committees popularized slogans such as "Non-Mulki Go Back" and "Idly Sambar Go Back".

question_text: The then Chief Minister N.T. Rama Rao appointed the three member committee with Jayabharata Reddy as the convener to report on which of the following aspects in Telangana?
explanation: In 1984, Chief Minister N.T. Rama Rao appointed a three-member officers' committee comprising Jayabharata Reddy (convener), Kamalanathan, and Umapathi to conduct a census/investigation of non-local government employees in Telangana violating the 1975 Presidential Order. The findings of this committee led to the issuance of the historic G.O. Ms. No. 610 in December 1985.

question_text: After Ramachandra Reddy of Pochampalli donated land for Bhoodan Movement, Vinoba Bhave constituted a three member committee for judicious distribution of lands among the poor. Who among the following was a member in that committee ?
explanation: Acharya Vinoba Bhave launched the Bhoodan Movement on April 18, 1951, at Pochampally after Vedire Ramachandra Reddy donated 100 acres of land. To oversee the management and equitable distribution of donated land, Vinoba Bhave formed a three-member committee consisting of Vedire Ramachandra Reddy, Sangam Laxmi Bai, and Ummethala Kesava Rao.

question_text: During whose administration in Hyderabad, Telugu and English languages replaced Urdu which hitherto was the State language ?
explanation: During the administration of M.K. Vellodi (who served as the Civil Administrator/Chief Minister of Hyderabad State from December 1949 to March 1952), English and regional languages like Telugu replaced Urdu as the official state languages of administration.

question_text: Who among the following was the Vice-President of Telangana Praja Samiti during 1969 Telangana Movement?
explanation: During the 1969 Telangana Agitation, the Telangana Praja Samiti (TPS) was established to spearhead the statehood movement. Ananthula Madan Mohan served as the President, while T.N. Sada Laxmi, a prominent Dalit leader, served as the Vice-President of TPS.

question_text: Which among the following was not part of the Gentlemen's Agreement ?
options: Telangana students had 3: 1 share in educational institutions.
Surplus revenue from Telangana to be spent for its own development.
Continued Mulki rules in government jobs.
Sale of landed property was controlled by Telangana Regional Council.
explanation: The Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 stipulated that educational facilities in Telangana be reserved for local students, but it did not specify a '3:1 share' ratio. Provisions included reserving Telangana surplus revenues for its own development, continuing Mulki rules for government jobs, and giving control over land sales to the Regional Council.

question_text: When the Telangana Political Joint Action Committee with all pro-Telangana Parties was formed with Prof. Kodanda Ram as the convener, which of the following parties did not join in it?
explanation: The Telangana Political Joint Action Committee (TJAC) was formed in December 2009 with Prof. M. Kodandaram as Chairman to unite various organizations and political parties for statehood. CPI(M) strictly opposed the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh and did not join the TJAC.

question_text: On December 28, 2012 U.P.A. government convened an All Party Meeting in Delhi on Telangana. Match the following parties with their leaders. List-1 (Parties) a. Congress b. Y.C.P. c. C.P.I. d. C.P.M. List-II (Leaders) i. K. Narayana & Gunda Mahesh ii. Raghavulu & Julakanti Ranga Reddy iii. Mysora Reddy & K.K. Mahendra Reddy iv. Suresh Reddy & Gade Venkata Reddy
explanation: In the All-Party meeting convened by Union Home Minister Sushilkumar Shinde on December 28, 2012, Congress was represented by K.R. Suresh Reddy & Gade Venkata Reddy; YSRCP by Mysora Reddy & K.K. Mahendra Reddy; CPI by K. Narayana & Gunda Mallesh (Mahesh); and CPM by B.V. Raghavulu & Julakanti Ranga Reddy.

question_text: Who among the following carved the 'Gun Park Martyrs Stupam' at Hyderabad in memory of those killed during 1969 agitation?
explanation: The iconic Telangana Martyrs Memorial (Amaraveerula Stupam) located at Gun Park, Hyderabad, was sculpted by prominent artist Ekka Yadagiri Rao. It was built to commemorate the 369 martyrs who died in police firing during the 1969 Jai Telangana Agitation.

question_text: Which one of the following statements is true with regard to the All Party Accord that arrived in January, 1969 at the initiatives of the Chief Minister Brahmananda Reddy on Mulki rules?
options: Those who obtained jobs by using fake Mulki certificates were to be transferred.
G.O. No. 36 was issued to retain all Non-Mulki as Andhra employees.
Persons employed in Telangana against the Mulki rules were to be regularized.
Mulki rules were to be applied even to autonomous organisations besides government departments.
explanation: During the All Party Accord convened by Chief Minister Kasu Brahmananda Reddy on January 18-19, 1969, leaders agreed that non-Mulkis illegally employed in Telangana should be repatriated by February 28, 1969, and Mulki rules should be extended to autonomous organizations, statutory bodies, and corporations alongside government departments.

question_text:
Assertion (A): There was great jubiliation of the people of Telangana over the Supreme Court Judgement on the status of Hyderabad city.
Reason (R): In October 2009 the Supreme Court ruled that Hyderabad should be treated as 'Free Zone'.
The correct answer is:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: The October 2009 Supreme Court judgment declared Hyderabad a 'Free Zone' regarding police recruitment, which diluted local employment protections under the Presidential Order. Instead of jubilation, this verdict caused massive outrage and widespread protests across Telangana, directly triggering the final phase of the statehood movement.

question_text: Match the following lists. List I (Ministers) (A) Dr. Virendra Kumar (B) Dr. Mahendra Nath Pandey (C) Dr. Jitendra Singh (D) Dr. Subrahmanyam Jaishankar List II (Portfolio) (I) Heavy Industries (II) Social Justice and empowerment (III) Science and Technology (IV) External Affairs The correct answer/
explanation: Dr. Virendra Kumar holds the portfolio of Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Mahendra Nath Pandey served as the Minister of Heavy Industries, Dr. Jitendra Singh oversees Science and Technology, and Dr. S. Jaishankar is the Minister of External Affairs.

question_text: On which day Lok Sabha accepted the separate Telangana State Bill ?
explanation: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill, 2014 was passed by the Lok Sabha on 18th February 2014. It was subsequently passed by the Rajya Sabha on 20th February 2014 and received Presidential assent on 1st March 2014.

question_text: P.K. Sinha recently stepped down from which position ?
explanation: Former Cabinet Secretary P.K. Sinha (Pradeep Kumar Sinha) was appointed as the Principal Advisor to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in September 2019, a role created specifically for him. He stepped down from this high-profile position in March 2021 citing personal reasons.

question_text: The Council of Ministers of Government of India is controlled by
options: Both Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha
explanation: According to Article 75(3) of the Constitution of India, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (House of the People) only. Therefore, the executive branch remains in power only as long as it enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha, which can remove it by passing a No-Confidence Motion.

question_text: Which of the following is not a function of Parliament?
options: Distribution of revenues between the Union and the States
explanation: The distribution of revenues between the Union and the States is a constitutional function assigned to the Finance Commission under Article 280, which makes recommendations to the President. Parliament does not distribute revenues, though it enacts tax laws, passes appropriations, and can legislate on inter-state water disputes under Article 262.

question_text: The Luni river, which originates in the pushkar valley of the Aravalli range, ends in which among the following?
explanation: The Luni River originates in the Pushkar Valley of the Aravalli Range near Ajmer. It is an inland drainage system that flows southwest through the Thar Desert and dissipates into the marshy lands of the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat without reaching the sea.

question_text: The total sanctioned strength of the Rajya Sabha is _________ members.
explanation: According to Article 80 of the Indian Constitution, the maximum sanctioned strength of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is fixed at 250 members. Out of these 250 members, 238 represent the States and Union Territories, while 12 are nominated by the President of India.

question_text: Ukai dam is situated across which of the following rivers?
explanation: The Ukai Dam, constructed across the Tapi River in the Tapi district of Gujarat, is the second largest reservoir in Gujarat after the Sardar Sarovar Dam. It is an earth-cum-masonry dam used for irrigation, power generation, and flood control.

question_text: As per the constitution of India, how many Members of Parliament (MPs) memberships are allotted for India Parliament?
explanation: Under the Constitution of India (Article 81 and Article 331), the maximum permitted strength of the Lok Sabha was fixed at 552 members (530 representing States, 20 representing Union Territories, and 2 nominated Anglo-Indians). The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 discontinued the nomination of Anglo-Indians.

question_text: Identify the following in which Money Bill cannot be introduced
explanation: According to Article 109(1) of the Indian Constitution, a Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha). It can only be introduced in the House of the People (Lok Sabha) on the prior recommendation of the President.

question_text: Which of the following is not a measure of Internal Security of India?
options: Preventing illegal activities in the country
Development of strong mechanism to fight against cybercrimes
Effective implementation of law against corruption
Protecting Indian citizens residing outside the country
explanation: Internal security refers to maintaining peace, law and order, and national integrity within a country's sovereign territorial boundaries (e.g., curbing cybercrime, preventing illegal activities, and fighting corruption). Protecting Indian citizens residing outside the country is a matter of foreign policy, diplomatic relations, and external affairs managed by the Ministry of External Affairs.

question_text: What is the title of Indian Health Ministry?
options: Ministry of health and child welfare
Ministry of health and family welfare
Ministry of home and family welfare
Ministry of home and child welfare
explanation: The official designation of the ministry responsible for health policy in India is the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW). It is headed by a Cabinet Minister and comprises two departments: the Department of Health and Family Welfare and the Department of Health Research.

question_text: The oath or affirmation by Indian President will be in the presence of _____.
explanation: According to Article 60 of the Indian Constitution, the oath or affirmation of the President of India is administered by the Chief Justice of India. In the absence of the Chief Justice of India, it is administered by the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court available.

question_text: Which Chief Justice of India became the acting President of India ?
explanation: Justice Mohammad Hidayatullah served as the Chief Justice of India and acted as the President of India from July 20, 1969 to August 24, 1969 following the resignation of Vice President V.V. Giri. He is the only Chief Justice of India to have served as the Acting President.

question_text: Who among the following Leaders of Telangana is known as "Telangana Bhagath Singh"?
explanation: Anabheri Prabhakar Rao was a key leader of the Telangana Peasant Armed Struggle in the Karimnagar region. Due to his intense revolutionary spirit and martyrdom at a young age fighting the Nizam's forces and Razakars, he is widely referred to as 'Telangana Bhagat Singh'.

question_text: How many members can be nominated to Rajya Sabha by using His/Her powers of President of India?
explanation: Under Article 80 of the Constitution of India, the President can nominate 12 members to the Rajya Sabha. These individuals are chosen for their special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as Literature, Science, Art, and Social Service.

question_text:
Match the following:
List - I
(a) Guru Shikhar Peak
(b) Dhuadhar waterfall
(c) Thalghat gap
(d) Coral reefs
List - II
(i) Lakshadweep islands
(ii) Western ghats
(iii) Narmada river
(iv) Aravallis
explanation: Guru Shikhar is the highest peak of the Aravalli Range (1,722 m). The Dhuandhar Falls are located on the Narmada River in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. Thalghat is an important mountain pass located in the Western Ghats connecting Mumbai and Nashik, and the Lakshadweep Archipelago consists of coral reef islands.

question_text: Assertion (A): The Parliament can legislate matters in State List in national interest. Reason (R): Rajya Sabha is part of Parliament. The correct answer is
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Under Article 249, Parliament can legislate on a State List subject if Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by a two-thirds majority in the national interest, making Assertion (A) true. Reason (R) is a correct factual statement regarding the composition of Parliament under Article 79, but it does not explain the specific procedure or justification under Article 249.

question_text:
Assertion (A): Collective responsibility of cabinet signifies unity and coordination among
members of the council of ministers
Reason (R) : It is the prerogative of the Prime Minister to select or drop a member of
the cabinet
The correct answer is
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Both statements are correct. Collective responsibility (Article 75) means that the cabinet functions as a single unified team jointly responsible to the Lok Sabha. The Prime Minister's authority to appoint or dismiss ministers is a key prime-ministerial privilege, but it is not the primary conceptual explanation of collective responsibility.

question_text: The newly appointed Chairperson of the Ethics Committee of Lok Sabha is
explanation: Senior leader Lal Krishna Advani was appointed as the Chairperson of the Ethics Committee of the 16th Lok Sabha. The Ethics Committee examines complaints relating to unethical conduct of members of the House and recommends appropriate action.

question_text:
Match the following
List - I
a) Sardar Sarovar dam
b) Highest mountain peak in South India
c) Todas
d) Copper
List - II
i) Anaimudi
ii) Agnigundala
iii) Narmada
iv) Nilgiri
explanation: Sardar Sarovar Dam is constructed across the Narmada River in Gujarat. Anaimudi (2,695 m) is the highest peak in Peninsular/South India. The Toda tribe resides primarily in the Nilgiri Hills, while Agnigundala in Andhra Pradesh is famous for its copper ore deposits.

question_text:
Match the following
List - I
River
a) Ganga
b) Brahmaputra
c) Godavari
d) Krishna
List - II
Tributary
i) Bhima
ii) Wainganga
iii) Teesta
iv) Kosi
explanation: Kosi is a major left-bank tributary of the Ganga; Teesta flows into the Brahmaputra; Wainganga is a prominent tributary of the Godavari river system; and Bhima is a major left-bank tributary of the Krishna river.

question_text: Match the following List - I Waterfall a) Dudhsagar b) Kapildhara c) Hogenakal d) Jog List - II River i) Mandovi ii) Narmada iii) Cauvery iv) Sharavaty
options: a: iv, b: iii, c: ii, d: i
a: i, b: ii, c: iii, d: iv
a: iv, b: iii, c: i, d: ii
a: i, b: ii, c: iv, d: iii
explanation: Dudhsagar Falls is located on the Mandovi River in Goa, Kapildhara Falls is formed by the Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh, Hogenakal Falls is on the Cauvery River in Tamil Nadu, and Jog Falls is formed by the Sharavathi River in Karnataka.

question_text: Match the following List - I River a) Cauvery b) Narmada c) Sabarmati d) Krishna List - II Source/origin i) Brahmagiri Hills ii) Amarkantak Plateau iii) Aravalli Hills iv) Western ghats
options: a: iv, b: iii, c: ii, d: i
a: i, b: ii, c: iii, d: iv
a: iv, b: iii, c: i, d: ii
a: i, b: ii, c: iv, d: iii
explanation: The Cauvery river originates in the Brahmagiri Hills of Karnataka, the Narmada river rises from the Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh, the Sabarmati river originates in the Aravalli Range in Rajasthan, and the Krishna river originates near Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats of Maharashtra.

question_text:
Match the following
List - I
Project
a) Rihind
b) Sileru
c) Mettur
d) Almatti
List - II
State
i) Karnataka
ii) Tamilnadu
iii) Andhra Pradesh
iv) Uttar Pradesh
explanation: Rihand Project is located in Uttar Pradesh on the Rihand River; Sileru Hydroelectric Project is located in Andhra Pradesh; Mettur Dam is constructed across the Cauvery River in Tamil Nadu; and Almatti Dam is built across the Krishna River in Karnataka.

question_text:
Read the following statements
a) River Brahmaputra is an antecedent river.
b) In Tibet, it is called as Tsangpo.
c) The important tributaries are Shyok, Shigar.
Which of the above statements is/are correct
explanation: The Brahmaputra is an antecedent river that originates in Tibet, where it is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo. Shyok and Shigar are major right-bank tributaries of the Indus River system, not the Brahmaputra.

question_text: The Coast Line of India excluding Islands is approximately:
explanation: The mainland coastline of India covers a distance of approximately 6,100 km. Including the island groups of Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar, the total length of India's coastline extends to 7,516.6 km.

question_text: Bhakra-Nangal project is constructed on the river
explanation: The Bhakra-Nangal Dam is one of India's earliest and largest multipurpose river valley projects, constructed on the Sutlej River near Bilaspur in Himachal Pradesh. The reservoir created by the dam is known as the Gobind Sagar lake.

question_text: Which of the following statements are correct? a) The chairman of Public Accounts Committee is always chosen from ruling party. b) The chairman of Public Accounts Committee is from opposition party. c) The chief function of Public Accounts Committee is to examine the report of CAG. d) The chairman of Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Vice President of India.
explanation: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) examines the annual audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG). Since 1967, a parliamentary convention mandates that the Chairman of PAC is chosen from the opposition party, appointed by the Speaker of Lok Sabha.

question_text: Which of the following statements are correct? a) S.B. Chavan was Deputy Prime Minister in Charan Singh's Government. b) Devi Lal was deputy Prime Minister in National Front Government. c) Y.B.Chavan was Deputy Prime Minister in Chandrashekar's Government. d) There are seven Deputy Prime Ministers so far.
explanation: Y.B. Chavan (not S.B. Chavan) was the Deputy PM in Charan Singh's government, making statement (a) incorrect. Devi Lal served as Deputy PM in both V.P. Singh's National Front government and Chandra Shekhar's government, making statement (b) correct and statement (c) incorrect. Statement (d) is correct as India has had 7 Deputy Prime Ministers till date: Sardar Patel, Morarji Desai, Jagjivan Ram, Charan Singh, Y.B. Chavan, Devi Lal, and L.K. Advani.

question_text: Who among the following submitted a memorandum to Fazal Ali Commission in July, 1954 when it came to Karimnagar requesting for Vishalandra
explanation: When the States Reorganisation Commission (Fazal Ali Commission) visited Karimnagar in July 1954 to gauge public opinion on state reorganization, Ananda Rao Thota submitted a memorandum requesting the formation of Vishalandra (merger of Telangana with Andhra State).

question_text: Which of the following Statements is not correct with regard to gentlemen agreement.
options: (1) To obtain jobs in Telangana, the Mulki rule has to be followed.
(2) Selling and buying of agricultureal lands in Telangana should be under the control of State Home Ministry.
(3) To look after the overall development of the region a Telangana Regional Committee should be appointed.
(4) Among the Ministers 60% should be from Andhra and 40% from Telangana.
explanation: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement signed in 1956, the sale and purchase of agricultural land in Telangana was to be controlled by the Telangana Regional Committee (Council), not the State Home Ministry. All other statements regarding Mulki rules, the 60:40 cabinet ratio, and the creation of a Telangana Regional Committee are accurate key clauses of the agreement.

question_text: The 10th July, 1968 was observed as
explanation: On July 10, 1968, Osmania University students observed 'Telangana Haameela Dinam' (Telangana Guarantees Day) to highlight the non-implementation of political and employment safeguards promised under the Gentlemen's Agreement. This protest acted as a major precursor to the 1969 Telangana Agitation.

question_text: In which of the following places 'Telangana Pranthiya Samithi' was formed.
explanation: The 'Telangana Pranthiya Samithi' was established in Illandu (Yellandu) in Khammam district during the early phases of the 1969 Telangana Agitation to demand the implementation of Mulki Rules and safeguards for local employees.

question_text: On which date in 1969 Mr. Krishna Murthy started fast unto death at Palvancha
explanation: On January 8, 1969, B.S. Krishnamurthy (an employee at Kothagudem Thermal Power Station) began an indefinite fast at Palvancha, demanding the implementation of Mulki Rules and Safeguards. Simultaneously, Annabathula Ravindranath started a fast unto death at Khammam, marking the historic onset of the 1969 Telangana Agitation.

question_text: Assertion (A): The State Government failed to impliment safeguards given to the people of Telangana in the gentlemen's agreemnet. Reason (R) : In 1969 students and youth thought securing the seperate state is the only solution to their problems. The correct answer is :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A) .
explanation: Both statements are historically correct. The AP State Government repeatedly violated the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement (Mulki rules, revenue allocation, public employment), making Assertion (A) true. As a direct consequence of these violations, student leaders in 1969 realized safeguards would never be respected, leading them to demand a separate Telangana state as the ultimate solution, making Reason (R) true. However, R describes the effect/consequence of A rather than its cause, so R is not the correct explanation of A.

question_text: Who among the following headed the full bench of the Supreme Court which set aside the G.O.No.: 36 in 1969.
explanation: In March 1969, a Constitution bench of the Supreme Court headed by Chief Justice M. Hidayatullah struck down G.O. No. 36 by declaring Section 3 of the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957 unconstitutional regarding Telangana. The court ruled that residential qualifications for public employment could only be prescribed for a whole State, not for a region within a State.

question_text: Which political party was the first to pass a resolution requesting the Government of India to form the Telangana State in 1969.
explanation: During the 1969 Jai Telangana Agitation, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh (Janasangh Party) was the first political party to formally pass a resolution demanding that the Government of India create a separate state of Telangana. Prominent leaders from the party advocated for regional political rights and safeguard implementations during this period.

question_text: In April, 1969 the Central government appointed a Committee headed by Justice Wanchoo and two members to study the problems of the Telangana employees and suggest solutions. Who were the other members.
explanation: In April 1969, as part of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's 8-Point Plan, the Central Government appointed a High-Powered Jurists Committee headed by former Chief Justice K.N. Wanchoo. Its other two distinguished legal expert members were M.C. Setalvad (former Attorney General of India) and Niren De (then Attorney General of India).

question_text: As part of the agitation for separate Telangana State 17th June, 1969 was observed as
explanation: During the 1969 Telangana Agitation, June 17, 1969 was observed as Women's Day ('Telangana Women's Day') across the region to mark the significant participation and leadership of women in the statehood struggle.

question_text: By which G.O. the Andhra Pradesh Government released Article 371 - D in October, 1975.
explanation: The Government of Andhra Pradesh issued G.O. Ms. No. 674 on October 20, 1975, to notify and enforce the Presidential Order under Article 371-D of the Constitution. This order instituted the local cadre system and direct recruitment regulations to implement the Six-Point Formula.

question_text: In which year the Government of Andhra Pradesh declared Jagityal and Sircilla as disturbed areas.
explanation: In October 1978, following the historic Jagtial Jaitrayatra peasant rally against feudal land lords, the Andhra Pradesh Government declared Jagtial and Sircilla talukas as 'disturbed areas' under the AP Suppression of Disturbances Act, 1948.

question_text: The State Government lifted the ban on People's war group in 2004 to facilitate
options: To have a database of the Naxalites
explanation: In June 2004, the newly elected Andhra Pradesh government lifted the ban on the People's War Group (PWG) and associated organizations specifically to facilitate peace talks with the government. These historic direct talks between government representatives and Naxalite leaders were held in October 2004.

question_text: Which Chief Minister abolished the Telangana Regional Development Board
explanation: Chief Minister N.T. Rama Rao abolished the Telangana Regional Development Board after coming to power in the 1980s. This decision was criticized by Telangana activists as it reduced regional statutory safeguards.

question_text:

(c) Telangana Maha Sabha
(d) Telangana Ikyavedika
List - II

question_text: Who among the following was the chief guest for the 'Simhagarjana' Public Meeting at Karimnagar in May, 2001.
explanation: On May 17, 2001, K. Chandrashekar Rao organised the historic 'Simhagarjana' public meeting in Karimnagar to launch the TRS movement for statehood. Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) leader Shibu Soren attended as the chief guest to extend solidarity to the Telangana cause.

question_text: In which place the first anniversary of the formation of the Telangana Rastra Samithi was held in April 2002.
explanation: The first anniversary (Plenary) of the formation of the Telangana Rashtra Samithi (TRS), founded by K. Chandrashekar Rao in April 2001, was held in Nalgonda in April 2002.

question_text: Who of the following did not attend the 'Jala Sadhana' meeting held at parade grounds, Secundarabad in January, 2003.
explanation: During the 'Jala Sadhana' meeting organized at Parade Grounds, Secunderabad in January 2003 to highlight irrigation water injustice to Telangana, prominent national leaders including Medha Patkar, Ramvilas Paswan, and Shibu Soren attended to express solidarity, whereas Sharad Yadav did not attend.

question_text: From which one of the following places TRS launched 'Pallebata' programme in October, 2003
explanation: The Telangana Rashtra Samithi (TRS) launched the 'Pallebata' (Path to Villages) outreach programme in October 2003 from Vemulawada in Karimnagar district. This movement aimed to interact directly with rural populations to build grassroot support and awareness for a separate Telangana state.

question_text: TRS organised an awareness programme 'Telangana Soyi' for
explanation: The Telangana Rashtra Samithi (TRS) organized 'Telangana Soyi' (Telangana Awareness) orientation training camps specifically for its party workers and cadres. These sessions aimed to equip party workers with historical facts, data regarding injustices in water, funds, and jobs, enabling them to effectively propagate the cause of Telangana statehood.

question_text: In which place in October, 2009 ‘Telangana Udyogula Garjana' was organised.
explanation: The 'Telangana Udyogula Garjana' (Telangana Employees' Garjana) was organized in Siddipet in October 2009. During this historic gathering, K. Chandrashekar Rao (KCR) declared his decision to launch an indefinite hunger strike with the famous slogan 'Telangana Thacho - KCR Chacho'.

question_text: TheTelangana Joint Action Committee was formed in 2009 on
explanation: The Telangana Joint Action Committee (TJAC) was formed on December 24, 2009, as an umbrella organization bringing together political parties and public organizations to lead the agitation for statehood. This was formed immediately after Union Home Minister P. Chidambaram's statement on December 23, 2009, which put the statehood process on hold. Professor M. Kodandaram was chosen as its convener/chairman.

question_text: From which one of the following places in Mahaboobnagar district B.J.P. started 'Telangana Poruyatra' in January, 2012.
explanation: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) launched the 22-day 'Telangana Poru Yatra', led by state BJP president G. Kishan Reddy, on January 19, 2012, from Krishna village in Mahabubnagar district to demand the creation of a separate Telangana state.

question_text: Srikantha Chari who Committed suicide for the cause of Telangana hailed from which village.
explanation: Kasoju Srikantha Chari was a prominent martyr of the Telangana statehood movement who self-immolated on 29 November 2009 at LB Nagar cross-roads. He hailed from Podichedu village in Mothkur mandal of Nalgonda district (present-day Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district).

question_text: On which date in 2013 O.U. Students Joint Action Committee Organised a big meeting called 'Telangana Yudha Bheri'
explanation: On September 22, 2013, the Osmania University Students Joint Action Committee (OU JAC) organized a massive public meeting named 'Telangana Yudha Bheri' at Nizam College Grounds, Hyderabad. The event was held to demand the early introduction and passage of the Telangana Statehood Bill in Parliament.

question_text: The President of India signed the Telangana Bill on
explanation: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill, 2014 was passed by the Lok Sabha on 18 February 2014 and by the Rajya Sabha on 20 February 2014. President Pranab Mukherjee gave his assent to the bill on 1 March 2014, making it an Act.

question_text: The Telangana Joint Action Committee was formed in 2009 on
explanation: The Telangana Joint Action Committee (TJAC) was formed on December 24, 2009, following the Union Government's statement on December 23 putting the statehood issue on hold. Professor M. Kodandaram was chosen as the Chairman of TJAC to spearhead the non-violent agitation across political and civil lines.

question_text:
Assertion (A): West flowing rivers of peninsular India have no deltas.
Reason (R) : These rivers do not carry any alluvial sediments.
Correct answer is :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: West-flowing peninsular rivers like Narmada and Tapi form estuaries rather than deltas because they flow through hard-rock rift valleys with steep gradients. While they do carry some sediments, the strong sea currents and high flow velocity prevent delta formation, making Assertion (A) true and Reason (R) false.

question_text:

(b) Zero hour is a typical Indian innovation in the field of parliamentary practice
(c) Judicial control over administrative acts stem from natural law
The correct answer is/are
options: (4) (a) and (c) are wrong and (b) is correct
explanation: Question Hour is the first hour of every parliamentary sitting dedicated to asking and answering questions. Zero Hour is an informal device introduced in 1962 as an Indian parliamentary innovation. Judicial control over administrative actions is grounded in natural law principles, such as natural justice and rule of law.

question_text:
Consider the following statements
Proclamation of 'State Emergency' under Art. 356 can continue beyond one year if
(a) The High Court of the State certifies that the situation in the State is very serious.
(b) The Governor of the State certifies that law and order situation is not under control.
(c) The Election Commission certifies that it is difficult to hold elections to the Assembly.
(d) The President is satisfied about the grave situation in the State through independent
investigation.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
explanation: According to the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1978, President's Rule under Article 356 can be extended beyond one year only if a National Emergency is in operation and the Election Commission certifies that general elections to the Legislative Assembly cannot be held due to difficulties.

question_text:
Read the following
A member of a House belonging to any political party shall be disqualified from being a Member
of House.
(a) If he is expelled from the party.
(b) If he has voluntarily given up his membership of such political party.
(c) If he votes or abstains from voting against the whip of the political party to which he belongs.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
explanation: Under the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law) of the Indian Constitution, a member incurs disqualification if they voluntarily give up political party membership or vote/abstain contrary to the party whip. Expulsion from a political party does not automatically disqualify an MP/MLA from the House under the Tenth Schedule.

question_text: Who among the following Presidents of India was associated with the Trade Union Movement in India ?
explanation: V.V. Giri, the 4th President of India, was a pioneering leader in the trade union movement in India. He served as the President of the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) twice and played a crucial role in founding the All India Railwaymen's Federation.

question_text: Find out the wrong pair concerned with Burgula Ramakrishna Rao Ministry in 1952.
options: Mehdi Nawaz Jung - Public Health and Public Works
M. Chenna Reddy - Agriculture and Planning
Shanker Dev - Education and Village Development
explanation: In the 1952 Burgula Ramakrishna Rao Cabinet of Hyderabad State, Shanker Dev served as the Minister for Social Welfare and Labour, not Education and Village Development. Education was initially under Phoolchand Gandhi and later Gopal Rao Ekbote.

question_text: Name the leader, who presided over ‘Telugu Bhasha Samithi’ meeting in July 1955 and asserted that “Culturally Vishalandra was already a reality”.
explanation: Madapati Hanumanth Rao, known as 'Andhra Pitamaha' for his role in establishing Andhra Jana Sangham and promoting Telugu literature in the Nizam State, presided over the Telugu Bhasha Samithi meeting in July 1955 and asserted that 'Culturally Vishalandra was already a reality'.

question_text: To oppose Sanjeeva Reddy ministry in 1963 who said “Andhra Government, seem to be a Government of the Reddys, for the Reddys and by the Reddys” ?
explanation: In 1963, prominent Dalit leader and former Constituent Assembly member S. Nagappa strongly criticized the Neelam Sanjiva Reddy administration for political hegemony, paraphrasing Abraham Lincoln's famous quote by stating that the Andhra Government seemed to be a 'Government of the Reddys, for the Reddys and by the Reddys'.

question_text: Before the States Re-organisation Commission many leaders expressed the opinion that the merger of an advanced region like Andhra with a backward region Hyderabad State would lead to
explanation: During the discussions around the States Reorganisation Commission (SRC), several prominent leaders, including Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, voiced concerns that merging the more politically, educationally, and financially advanced Andhra state with Telangana (Hyderabad State) would result in 'internal colonisation' and exploitation of the latter's resources.

explanation: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi announced the Five Point Formula on November 27, 1972, following the Supreme Court judgment on Mulki Rules. question_text: Arrange the names of the following Speakers of Lok Sabha in a chronological order of the office they held: a. K.S. Hegde b. Rabi Ray c. Balram Jakhar d. Shivaraj Patil e. P.A. Sangma Choose the correct order/answer/

question_text: Examine the following statements with regard to office of Speaker of Lok Sabha : A. Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy was Speaker of the Lok Sabha twice. B. Speaker of the Lok Sabha always comes from the ruling party. C. K.S. Hegde was succeeded by Balram Jakhar as the Speaker. D. The Protem Speaker of the 16th Lok Sabha was Jyotiriditya Scindia. explanation: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy served twice as the Speaker of Lok Sabha (4th and 6th Lok Sabha). K.S. Hegde served as Speaker during 1977-1980 and was succeeded by Balram Jakhar in 1980. question_text: Which one among the following is not true with regard to joint sitting of the Parliament?
options: In the absence of Speaker, Deputy Speaker presides over it.
In the absence of Deputy Sepaker, Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha presides over it.
In the absence of Deputy Chairman, the Chairman of Rajya Sabha presides over it.
It is presided over by Speaker.
explanation: The Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice-President of India) never presides over a joint sitting of Parliament because he is not a member of either House. In the absence of the Deputy Chairman, a member agreed upon by the members present at the sitting presides.

question_text: Which one among the following is not correct?
options: President of India with the consent of the Governor can entrust any matter related to executive power of the Union to the State Government.
Governor unconditionally can entrust any matter related to executive power of the State to Government of India with its consent.
President of India without the consent of the Governor can entrust any matter related to executive power of the Union to the State Government.
Governor can entrust conditionally any matter related to executive power of the State to Government of India with its consent.
explanation: Under Article 258(1) of the Constitution, the President can entrust Union executive functions to a State Government only with the consent of that State's Governor/Government. Executive entrustment without consent is not permitted for the President, although Parliament may do so by law under Article 258(2).

question_text:

Parameswaran (Literature & Education). Therefore, statements A, D, and F are correct.

question_text:
